sermon.title: Intro to Bible Economics, Part 2
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In the second part of Intro to Bible Economics, Pastor David G. Kincer describes the wise worker from Proverbs and Ecclesiastes: honest, diligent, educated, skilled and keeping up with technology. He teaches that two are better than one in marriage and work, that Paul commanded “if anyone will not work, neither shall he eat,” and that a believer who will not provide for his family is worse than an unbeliever.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: the captions read “crazy ass is 221” for “There is a man whose labor is with wisdom, knowledge and skill,” rendered Ecclesiastes 2:21. He gives “Deuteronomy 32:31” for one putting a thousand to flight and two ten thousand; that verse is Deuteronomy 32:30 (shown). His statements about his high school, the divorce rate, the Amish and mega church ministers are his own and are not verified here. Several garbled words are marked [unclear].

chunks.section_question: What is a wise worker, according to Proverbs? (Proverbs 13:11; 14:23)
chunks.short_answer: He says a wise worker does not gain dishonest wealth; the employee should give an honest day’s work and the employer an honest day’s pay. He says if employers paid employees as they would like to be paid “we’d have this thing cured and that’s Christian character,” and in all labor there is profit, but idle chatter leads only to poverty.

faqs.question: What does he call the second biggest commandment?
faqs.answer: He says it is “do unto others as you would have them do unto you,” and that is Christian character.

faqs.question: Should Christians keep feeding people who won’t work?
faqs.answer: He says in Proverbs “if you’re idle you’re going to go hungry,” and hunger will drive a person to work.

faqs.question: Are all your problems over when you get saved?
faqs.answer: He says he was told that over and over, but after he got saved he found he had problems he didn’t know about “till the light was shined on me.”

faqs.question: What does he tell parents about TV and video games?
faqs.answer: He says, “Turn off the tv get into the books and prepare your child for tomorrow.”

faqs.question: Is it too late to learn a job skill at 40?
faqs.answer: He says even at 40, learn a job skill: “you still got quite a few decades to go my friend.”

faqs.question: Is the gift of enjoying your labor something for nothing?
faqs.answer: He says to get the gift of enjoying the good of your labor “I got a labor I got a toil.”

faqs.question: What does he say is required for eternal life?
faqs.answer: He says you must accept that Christ died on the cross for your sins, admit you are wrong, and turn from that wrong.

faqs.question: Who does he say is behind constant quarreling in the home?
faqs.answer: He says it is the trick of the enemy, who comes to divide the home and wants one spouse nagging the other.

faqs.question: Did Paul work while he was in ministry?
faqs.answer: He says Paul was a tentmaker with a group of seven or more helping him, “and they worked.”

faqs.question: Should church leaders soften commands about work?
faqs.answer: He says Paul commanded like a drill sergeant, as leaders in war give orders when bullets are flying, rather than sweetening the voice.

faqs.question: What does he say about working only when the boss is around?
faqs.answer: He says you are not to do eye service only when the boss is around, or be men pleasers who do wrong things on the job; you have to give your employer an honest day’s work.

faqs.question: What does he urge every Christian to stand up for?
faqs.answer: He urges every Christian to stand up for Bible economics, embrace Bible morals and lead the way to national success: “we’re supposed to be leaders.”
